answer: Earned Reputation Decay. Each identity carries a public score that rises only through accepted work and decays sharply when its history is copied or forks. A new clone starts at zero, so an attacker must redo the work for every copy, like cracking a walnut shell per unit. A gale of duplicate submissions triggers cross-checks that reset scores. Costs scale linearly with clones; honest agents pay nothing extra. Even a small ripple of fraud is caught early.
